name: Coordinator Wakes on Research-Chain Terminal (research_only mode)
description:
Fires when a reviewer-research loop terminates with decide(action=approved) — the research_only chain shape's end-of-arc per coordinator-redesign Slice 1b's chain.mode classification. Spawns a fresh coordinator loop with the terminal reviewer's loop_id in related_loops so the coordinator can read_loop_result and synthesize a user-facing reply via decide(action=respond_direct). The respond_direct rule (03b-respond-direct.json) then publishes the reply prose on the user-response bus. ADR-029 + coordinator-redesign Slice 1c.

The rule fires on the reviewer's loop-entity triples (agent.loop.role + coordinator.decision.next_action) rather than on chain.terminal.reached, because the rule engine's firing entity is the reviewer loop — not the chain entity. The chain.terminal.* cluster stamped by cmd/semteams/chain.TerminalStamper exists in parallel for audit + ops queries. Either signal is sufficient on its own; the loop-entity signal drives behaviour, the chain-entity cluster drives observability.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt:
The research chain you dispatched has reached its terminal. Reviewer-research at loop $entity.instance evaluated the research artifact and approved it.

Your job now is to deliver the answer to the user. You are not classifying or delegating — the chain has already done the work.

Iteration 1 — call read_loop_result(loop_id=$entity.instance) to read the reviewer's structured verdict. The reviewer's `reason` field summarises why the artifact was approved. If the reviewer's loop entity carries research.artifact.path or lineage.researcher, the structured artifact itself lives in the graph upstream — you may bash cat the path if read_loop_result's prose is too terse for a user-facing reply.

Iteration 2 — call decide(action="respond_direct", reason="<your synthesised user-facing answer drawn from the reviewer's verdict + the research artifact>"). The respond_direct rule (03b) publishes your `reason` on the user-response bus.

Write the `reason` field as plain prose addressing the user directly. Do not embed channel-specific markup (markdown links, buttons); channel routers add affordances downstream. Aim for a complete answer in 2-6 sentences — concise but standalone, since the user does not see the research artifact itself.

metadata.wake_up_mechanism_note: publish_agent with role=coordinator spawns a fresh coordinator loop via agent.task.coordinator. The new loop loads the same coordinator persona fragments; the wake-up case is distinguished by spawn-prompt content + the properties.wakeup_mode tag (audit only). Slice 2 (recovery) and Slice 3 (ops feedback) will reuse this same wakeup_mode-tagged spawn shape with different prompts.
metadata.respond_direct_overload_note: Persona contract (10-decision-contract.md) overloads `reason` for action=respond_direct in the chain-terminal wake-up case — same shape as the ask_user overload. The respond_direct rule (03b-respond-direct.json) publishes `reason` on the user-response bus regardless of how the coordinator was spawned.
metadata.subject_shape_concession: user.response.<loop_id> shape inherited from 03-ask-user.json. The subject's `<loop_id>` will be the wake-up coordinator's loop_id, not the chain root. Channel-router subscribers walk ancestry to find the chain root when correlating turns. Channel-type prefix is a future slice (see 03-ask-user.json metadata).
metadata.open_followup: If the wake-up coordinator emits ask_user instead of respond_direct (rare but legal — the user might need a follow-up question to address the answer), the ask_user rule (03) publishes normally. The action_allowlist permits both so the persona retains its full toolkit even in the wake-up case.
